chunks: The Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Abu al-Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from 'Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from 'Umar ibn Udhaynah and Ibn Bukayr, from Zurarah, from Abi Ja'far عليه السلام, who said:
Nothing of the recitation and the du'a is recorded except what he makes himself hear.

key_terms.أَسْمَعَ: caused to hear, meaning he made audible
key_terms.الْقِرَاءَةِ: the liturgical recitation, especially in salat (prayer)
key_terms.نَفْسَهُ: his own self, indicating the minimum audible level
key_terms.يُكْتَبُ: is counted or recorded as valid

ai.seo_question: Does recitation in prayer and du'a count if a person does not make himself hear it?
ai.summary: This hadith states that recitation and du'a count only when a person audibly makes himself hear them. It indicates a legal requirement in acts of worship that verbal utterance must at least reach one's own hearing.
